front: What is the range of a dataset?
back: R = L − S, where L is the largest value and S is the smallest value. Quick measure of spread but ignores intermediate values.
M.D.(x̄) = Σ|xᵢ − x̄|/n, where x̄ = mean and |xᵢ − x̄| = absolute deviations.
M.D.(x̄) = Σfᵢ|xᵢ − x̄|/N, where N = Σfᵢ is the total frequency.

front: Why is variance preferred over mean deviation?
back: Absolute values are not algebraically convenient (hard to differentiate). Squared deviations overcome this limitation.
σ² = (1/N)Σ(xᵢ − x̄)². Always non-negative. σ = √(σ²) is the standard deviation.
uᵢ = (xᵢ − a)/h. Mean: x̄ = a + h(Σfᵢuᵢ/N). Variance: σ² = h²[Σfᵢuᵢ²/N − (Σfᵢuᵢ/N)²].

front: Effect of shifting data by constant c
back: Mean shifts by c. Variance, standard deviation, and mean deviation all remain unchanged.

front: Effect of multiplying data by constant k
back: Mean multiplied by k. Variance multiplied by k². Standard deviation multiplied by |k|.
CV = (σ/x̄) × 100. A percentage measure of dispersion. Higher CV means greater relative spread.
If all values are equal, σ = 0 (zero spread). Deviations from the mean are all zero.
